About AI discoveries in biology

This selection contains 661 catalog entries dated 17 Jan 2020 to 15 Nov 2026. 661 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

13 Nov 2026Stanford University

Antibody design across observed and forecasted antigenic evolution

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The Germinal Multi preprint abstract reports antibodies designed against several antigen variants at once. Experimental screens of tens of designs per campaign found binders to resistance-associated EGFR variants and neutralizers of historical SARS-CoV-2 variants, including variants withheld from design. Redesign of BD55-1205 restored neutralization of a forecast-guided engineered escape variant while retaining parental-variant activity. The escape result concerns an engineered variant, not a demonstrated future circulating strain. Review is limited to the abstract and original-server metadata.

Technology: Germinal Multi (computational antibody design framework); evolutionary forecasting model

Editorial relevance 67 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Preprint · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Germinal Multi computationally optimized one antibody paratope against multiple antigen variants, and an evolutionary forecasting model guided construction of an escape variant and antibody redesign.
Test and result
Tens of designs per campaign were screened experimentally; designs bound EGFR variants and neutralized SARS-CoV-2 variants, including variants withheld from the design process.
Limitation / still unknown
Review limited to the indexed abstract and publication metadata; full-paper methods and additional limitations were not assessed.

9 Nov 2026Harvard Medical School; Harvard College; New York Genome Center; Rush Alzheimer’s Disease Center, Rush University

TriSCOPE links cell-type-specific Alzheimer’s expression programs to inherited risk loci

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: TriSCOPE combined cell-level predictive modeling, donor-aware differential expression and pseudotime analysis across six single-nucleus RNA-sequencing datasets (about 4.2 million nuclei from 627 donors). It identified cell-type-specific predictively expressed genes that were often missed by univariate differential-expression analysis; conditional GWAS–eQTL colocalization supported 27 gene–cell-type pairs at Alzheimer’s risk loci, including pairs without significant differential expression. Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.

Technology: TriSCOPE, using LightGBM-based multivariate predictive modeling integrated with differential expression and pseudotime analysis

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The supervised machine-learning branch prioritized gene-expression features that predicted clinical Alzheimer’s diagnosis within cell types, conditional on demographics and APOE genotype. The study integrated those model-ranked features with donor-aware differential expression, pseudotime and GWAS–eQTL colocalization to nominate genetically supported cell-type programs.
Test and result
Selected gene signals and analytical branches were compared across independent cohorts.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a computational reanalysis of previously published, post-mortem cross-sectional datasets; it did not collect new tissue or perform perturbation experiments. The authors state the framework is for feature discovery rather than clinical prognosis, cannot establish temporal ordering, and requires functional perturbation studies to distinguish pathogenic drivers from protective or reactive signals. The reported cell-level AUCs are modest and should not be presented as patient-level diagnostic performance.

Generative design of de novo AAV vectors with unique serological profiles

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The preprint abstract reports a variational autoencoder trained on natural AAV sequences to generate capsids. More than 255 designs were synthesized and tested in vitro. Seven transduced human cells at over 50% efficiency; four of those avoided neutralization by every AAV-reactive human serum sample tested, at the reported NT50 threshold below 1:50. This establishes in-vitro capsid properties, not in-vivo delivery or clinical efficacy. Review is limited to the abstract and original-server metadata.

9 Nov 2026University of Sydney; Children’s Hospital at Westmead; Macquarie University; Translational Genomics Research Institute; Baylor College of Medicine; Emory University

Learned blood-omics factors track Rett syndrome status and severity in a small cohort

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Unsupervised integration of four blood-omics measurements identified a disease-associated molecular factor and a second factor correlated with clinical severity in nine people with Rett syndrome and eight controls. The learned factors connect measurements across molecular layers, but remain exploratory within-cohort associations. They are not validated diagnostic tests, causal disease mechanisms or demonstrated treatment-response markers.

Technology: MOFA2 unsupervised multi-omics latent-factor learning

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
MOFA2 learned shared variation across transcript, protein, phosphorylation and metabolite measurements, enabling the represented cross-layer disease and severity-associated factor analysis beyond separate differential-expression tests.
Test and result
Four matched molecular-data layers from nine Rett syndrome participants and eight controls were integrated using MOFA2 latent-factor learning. The main computational Methods specify normalized inputs, participant-identifier joins and associations between factor scores and clinical severity. Factor 1 separated the sampled clinical groups; Factor 2 correlated with severity among the nine affected participants, with reported Spearman rho 0.77 and nominal p 0.016.
Limitation / still unknown
Seventeen people and nine severity observations are too few to establish generalizable biomarker performance. Factor selection and severity association used the same cohort, without held-out diagnostic evaluation or demonstrated multiplicity-adjusted confirmation of the severity result. Age, cell composition, medication, diet and systemic physiology may influence molecular profiles; peripheral blood does not directly establish brain mechanisms. Orthogonal measurement of an individual metabolite does not independently validate the learned latent factors. No longitudinal response-to-treatment or causal effect was tested.

9 Nov 2026Department of Ophthalmology, Byers Eye Institute, Stanford University School of Medicine, Stanford, United States

Dual-feature selectivity enables bidirectional coding in visual cortical neurons.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Macaque V1/V4 and mouse visual-cortex neurons showed dual-feature selectivity: elevated-baseline neurons were excited by preferred features and systematically suppressed by distinct non-preferred features, with graded responses across a continuum. Model predictions were tested against held-out images and recorded neuronal responses; reported selectivity patterns were cross-checked across models, macaque areas/species and mouse cortex. The authors note in-silico limitations, small animal counts, and lower V4 model coverage (52% retained).

Technology: Deep neural network functional digital twins predicted neuron responses to natural images, enabling systematic selectivity analysis over 1.2 million images and model-guided stimulus tests.

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution

Test and result
Macaque V1/V4 and mouse visual-cortex neurons showed dual-feature selectivity: elevated-baseline neurons were excited by preferred features and systematically suppressed by distinct non-preferred features, with graded responses across a continuum.
Limitation / still unknown
Model predictions were tested against held-out images and recorded neuronal responses; reported selectivity patterns were cross-checked across models, macaque areas/species and mouse cortex. The authors note in-silico limitations, small animal counts, and lower V4 model coverage (52% retained).

Source checked · editorial details

Source type: paper. Paper: not linked in this catalog; this does not mean no paper exists.

Review date: 22 Nov 2026. Review scope: Read the primary eLife full text (Methods and Results; PMC full text) and checked the Europe PMC record. The authors trained functional digital twins on macaque V1/V4 and mouse visual-cortex recordings, validated response predictions on held-out images and direct in-vivo responses, then screened 1.2 million natural images. They report that many neurons encode both preferred-stimulus excitation and systematic suppression by distinct non-preferred features, with the pattern also seen in mice and across cortical areas. First publication was 2026-11-09; the active and archived snapshots contain no exact matching DOI/title/result. The models provide the large-scale stimulus search; core recordings and cross-model/in-vivo checks support the result. Caveats: analyses rely substantially on in-silico responses, only two macaques per area, and high-confidence filtering retained 52% of V4 neurons..

Methods/Results show ChAI-Net is a deep CNN trained on ~3.4 million 2,048-bp windows of mouse embryonic stem-cell SAMOSA single-molecule footprint data to predict 16-bp-resolution co-accessibility maps. 30 Oct 2026Xinjiang Medical University; People’s Hospital of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region

Learned coronary-fat radiomics stratifies an angina-dominated clinical endpoint

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A learned coronary-fat radiomics score was associated with subsequent cardiovascular readmissions in 578 prospectively collected patients. The composite endpoint was overwhelmingly worsening or unstable angina, with only two myocardial infarctions. The source reports an adjusted hazard ratio of 2.611 between score-defined groups; cutoff selection in the follow-up cohort and uncertain temporal model locking limit its interpretation as independent prognostic validation.

Technology: LASSO radiomics selection and stochastic-gradient-descent classifier of pericoronary fat CT features

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Supervised feature selection and the learned radiomics classifier combined CT texture and intensity measurements into the score used for the represented clinical event-association analysis. The segmentation software is labeled AI-assisted by the source, but its undisclosed architecture is not invented here.
Test and result
A matched retrospective development set included 200 event cases and 200 controls, with a random 80:20 split and fivefold cross-validation. LASSO selected fourteen radiomics features and an SGD classifier was selected from five classifiers. A separate prospectively collected cohort included 578 patients with mean follow-up 29.17 months: 129 readmissions for worsening stable or unstable angina and two myocardial infarctions. Events were verified from records/interviews and adjudicated by two blinded cardiovascular specialists. The source reports adjusted HR 2.611, 95% CI 1.806–3.775, for score-defined high versus low groups.
Limitation / still unknown
The Methods describe ROC-derived cutoffs in the prospective cohort, so the reported risk separation is not a fully independent test of a prespecified threshold. Five-year retrospective outcome ascertainment overlaps the chronology of 2022 validation enrollment; model locking before those outcomes was not established. Matched case-control sampling and a restricted age-based clinical comparator limit calibration and comparative claims. Feature preprocessing isolation is incompletely specified. Single-center data and an angina-dominated composite do not establish broad hard-event prediction, causal inflammation mechanisms or clinical intervention benefit.

19 Jun 2026University of Pennsylvania

Deep learning identifies antimicrobial peptides hidden in prion-related proteins

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: APEX 1.1 screened 19.3 million peptide fragments from 2,897 prion-related proteins and identified 1,179 candidate antimicrobial peptides, termed prionins. Among 75 synthesized candidates, 59 inhibited at least one tested bacterial strain; two selected peptides reduced Acinetobacter baumannii burden in a mouse skin-abscess model. The study shows that prion-related sequences can yield experimentally active antimicrobial fragments, but does not show that these peptides are naturally released or function as host-defense agents in their source organisms.

15 Jun 2026Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory; Johns Hopkins University

Fung-AI prioritizes peptides with measured antifungal activity

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Fung-AI combines a generative adversarial network with learned antifungal and hemolysis classifiers to select peptides for testing. The study first tested five peptides from separate clusters; activity of peptide 40 prompted testing of eight more members from cluster 17. Five of the nine tested cluster-17 peptides inhibited Fusarium graminearum, a post-selection cluster-specific outcome—not a general 5/13 model hit rate. Four peptides showed activity against Candida albicans, while none inhibited C. auris up to 500 μg/mL. The paper’s HepG2 cytotoxicity statements are internally inconsistent for peptide 48 and peptide 65, and peptide 12 and 40 have reported cytotoxicity; these assays establish neither human safety nor clinical efficacy.

Finding: RFdiffusion-based de novo binder design and experimental screening produced synthetic proteins that inhibited three bacterial defense systems: Thoeris and Avs1 in Bacillus subtilis assays, and DdmDE in Vibrio cholerae. Family AlphaFold: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 67 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
RFdiffusion generated candidate binder backbones for selected target sites in the Thoeris, Avs1 and DdmDE defense proteins; ProteinMPNN designed sequences and AlphaFold-based co-folding/scoring prioritized candidates for experiments. The selected synthetic binders were tested for defense inhibition, direct interactions and ability to restore phage infection or plasmid retention. The measured anti-defense functions and engineered-phage outcomes are the paper-specific results enabled by AI-guided protein design.
Test and result
RFdiffusion-based de novo binder design and experimental screening produced synthetic proteins that inhibited three bacterial defense systems: Thoeris and Avs1 in Bacillus subtilis assays, and DdmDE in Vibrio cholerae.
Limitation / still unknown
These are laboratory proof-of-concept results in three bacterial defense systems and specific strains; they do not demonstrate therapeutic phage efficacy in animals or humans. Binder success was low relative to the computationally designed candidate sets, and the authors note that a verified binder may not work against homologous defense proteins. The native V. cholerae result was tested for plasmid retention, not general transformation across clinical isolates. The earlier bioRxiv version is the same study and is not a separate record.

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned forest prioritized measured metabolic features and combined them into the represented tissue-classification pattern; pathway enrichment alone is not the AI-enabled finding.
Test and result
The source measured fifteen early-onset tumors, fifteen later-onset tumors and fifteen adjacent-normal tissue specimens. Differential filtering produced 141 features, followed by random-forest prioritization of ten. Tenfold cross-validation repeated ten times yielded a reported mean early-onset discrimination AUC 0.916. A separate public transcriptomic dataset was used only for pathway-level comparison, not validation of the metabolic classifier.
Limitation / still unknown
Feature filtering/selection isolation within cross-validation was not established, making performance optimistic. Specimen-level versus patient-level separation of adjacent tissues was not reconstructed, and age, stage or other cohort differences may explain some signals. Metabolite annotations were mainly database matches without universal authentic-standard confirmation. No independent classifier validation or clinical screening utility was demonstrated. Transcript and metabolite measurements came from different people, so shared pathway enrichment does not establish individual gene–metabolite coupling, causal pathology or treatment targets.

Limitation / still unknown
The classifier operated at a 33% false-discovery rate; the 135 ion traces were putatively annotated, and only four of 22 reconstructed reaction stoichiometries were experimentally validated. Therefore the full 11% result is a set of candidate activities, not 11% independently confirmed enzyme functions. The RihB activities were prompted by a low-confidence potassium-thymidine-adduct trace and then tested directly with purified enzyme; they should be distinguished from the classifier’s higher-confidence hit set.

The functional experiment is a human neuroblastoma cell model exposed to α-synuclein preformed fibrils, not a clinical or in-vivo therapeutic demonstration. TPP1 is a candidate therapeutic target, not a validated treatment.

The primary Methods retained 4,536 eligible SEER records and split them 3,175:1,361 for training/internal testing. Feature screening and tenfold tuning were described within training. AI-guided subtilisin variants improve aqueous amide formation

Finding: The study reports that wild-type subtilisin BPN′ directly catalyzed condensation of free carboxylic acids and amines in aqueous PBS (pH 8, 40 °C), forming a peptide-bond amide without stoichiometric coupling reagents. The top triple mutant N155G/N218D/M222Q had reported relative activity of 753 ± 14% of wild type and also coupled biotin to a peptide fragment in water, extending beyond peptide–peptide ligation.

Technology: Random forests combining receptor–ligand expression features for assay-response classification

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Random forests learned nonlinear combinations of expression features linked to measured assay outcomes, enabling the observed distinction between cancer-specific and pan-cancer response prediction. Generic classifier benchmarks alone and untested clinical benefit are not the admitted claim.
Test and result
The source analyzed 76 distinct NK-cell samples against fourteen ovarian-cancer cell lines, then extended modeling across cancers. Random forests used 70:30 training/test partitions, ten-fold grid-search tuning and twenty random repetitions. A separate pan-cancer test set produced AUC 0.638 and accuracy 63.52%; source-reported breast- and gastric-cancer models reached separate-test AUCs 0.831 and 0.865. The result concerns measured assay response and its cancer-dependent generalization.
Limitation / still unknown
Random tumor–immune-cell pair partitions do not establish complete donor/cell-line independence; shared entities could affect apparent generalization. Upstream feature screening isolation and supplementary pair-level reconstruction were not verified. Five patient-derived AML samples and one treated patient do not establish prospective clinical efficacy or broad therapy-selection utility. Operational cell preparation, experimental manipulation and treatment protocols were not adjudicated.

29 Sep 2025Zhejiang University; Harbin Genars Technology; GenVista Technology

Learned eleven-gene melanoma score associates with survival in public expression cohorts

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A penalized survival-model pipeline produced an eleven-gene melanoma score associated with observed survival in public expression cohorts. Model selection used both internal testing and an additional cohort, so the latter is not an untouched external test. The represented result is a retrospective prognostic association, without establishing novel cell types, causal tumor biology or improved treatment decisions.

Technology: Scissor phenotype-linked feature selection followed by LASSO Cox and ridge survival modeling

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Phenotype-linked selection and penalized learned survival modeling combined expression measurements into the represented score, enabling observed survival stratification beyond generic clustering or pathway enrichment.
Test and result
The source linked single-cell data to bulk survival data using Scissor, derived prognosis-related gene sets and compared seventy-two model combinations. It selected a LASSO Cox/ridge eleven-gene score using average performance across testing datasets. The paper reports a survival-group association in GSE65904, described as 215 samples, with modest time-dependent discrimination.
Limitation / still unknown
Outcome-informed upstream filtering and use of testing cohorts to choose the final model compromise independent validation. The paper reports 469 available TCGA records but a different final subgroup count in discussion, without a reconstructed participant flow here. Reported survival-time labels differ between text and figure captions, so exact time-specific AUCs are not adopted. Single-cell cluster labels, including the claimed MITF-positive T-cell population, were not independently authenticated as new biological cell types. Many individual genes already have melanoma associations. No causal mechanism, treatment benefit or clinical decision utility was demonstrated.

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

AI contribution
XGBoost learned residual prediction patterns and adjusted the prior pharmacokinetic estimates; comparison with measured subsequent concentrations supplies the specific clinical validation result. The pre-existing Bayesian model/dashboard alone is not treated as a new discovery.
Test and result
The source analyzed 292 successive-concentration pairs from 93 patients aged 2–22 years. XGBoost learned prediction errors using clinical features and prior drug measurements. Limitation / still unknown

Correlation-based feature selection and algorithm comparisons may affect internal performance; independent final evaluation was absent. Low concentrations below quantification were excluded. The target-cell killing experiment used engineered CD8+ cells in vitro and three donors; no animal or patient treatment outcome was tested. Protein abundance prediction used limited cell and immune-subset datasets, and model feature importance is not itself causal evidence. The assay supports effects for the tested synthetic 3′UTRs and CDK4-specific TCR in the reported system, not all proteins or therapeutic settings.

Deep-learning models predicted plant gene expression from regulatory DNA and used interpretability/occlusion and in-silico editing to identify promoter/5′UTR sequences likely to alter expression. The editing-plasticity predictions guided CRISPR-Cas9 targeting of ZmVTE4; the resulting four-base 5′UTR deletion was experimentally linked to increased gene expression and maize-kernel α-tocopherol. This is a measured crop-specific molecular/metabolite outcome, not merely an in-silico editing proposal.

11 Dec 2024Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics; Center for Systems Biology Dresden; TU Dresden Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life

PICNIC machine learning predictions revealed previously poorly characterized human proteins in cellular condensates

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The PICNIC gradient-boosting model ranked proteins for membership in biomolecular condensates using sequence-pattern and AlphaFold2-derived structural features. To test its predictions, researchers expressed 24 poorly characterized human proteins in U2OS cells: 21 formed mesoscale fluorescent foci, and 18 met the paper’s high-confidence condensate threshold. The experiments mapped examples to cytoplasmic bodies, nuclear bodies, nucleoli or P-bodies; for example, TYW5 and RAD51AP1 showed distinct localization patterns. Across the tested set, the authors found condensate localization was not limited to highly disordered proteins.

Technology: PICNIC, a gradient-boosting machine-learning classifier using protein sequence co-occurrence patterns, sequence complexity/disorder features and AlphaFold2-derived structural features

Family AlphaFold: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PICNIC scored human proteins for likely cellular-condensate membership and selected poorly characterized positive predictions for experimental testing. Its rankings directly guided the 24-protein U2OS localization validation; the model was built to predict condensate members (including clients), not only proteins that self-drive phase separation.
Test and result
To test its predictions, researchers expressed 24 poorly characterized human proteins in U2OS cells: 21 formed mesoscale fluorescent foci, and 18 met the paper’s high-confidence condensate threshold.
Limitation / still unknown
The experimental test used fluorescently tagged proteins expressed in U2OS cells, so observed localization may depend on expression level, tag, cell type or condition. The study did not establish each protein’s endogenous localization or biological function; the authors explicitly state that condensate localization alone makes no functional claim. Three of 24 proteins did not form detectable mesoscale foci, and three additional results were low-confidence under the paper’s size threshold. This is targeted experimental validation of model-selected candidates, not an independently replicated atlas.

9 Dec 2024Northeast Normal University; Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Exeter; John Innes Centre; Alan Turing Institute

PlantRNA-FM identifies translation-associated RNA motifs and structure motifs in plants

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The PlantRNA-FM model, pretrained on sequence and predicted RNA structure from 1,124 plant transcriptomes, identified 5′-UTR motifs associated with translation efficiency across plant transcriptomes. Reporter assays in plants tested selected predictions: mutating a high-translation-associated RNA secondary-structure motif reduced measured translation efficiency by up to 5.3-fold, while disrupting a model-prioritized low-translation-associated RNA G-quadruplex motif increased it by up to 5.8-fold. The paper reports the rG4 motifs as translation-repressive, consistent with prior evidence on individual rG4s; the transcriptome-wide model prioritization and tested instances are the scoped findings here.

Technology: PlantRNA-FM, an interpretable RNA foundation model integrating RNA sequence and predicted structure

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PlantRNA-FM was pretrained with plant RNA sequence and structure data, then fine-tuned on translation-efficiency data. An attention-contrast interpretation framework prioritized 5′-UTR sequence/structure motifs associated with translation; researchers tested selected motif predictions by mutating reporter constructs and measuring translation efficiency in plants.
Test and result
Reporter assays in plants tested selected predictions: mutating a high-translation-associated RNA secondary-structure motif reduced measured translation efficiency by up to 5.3-fold, while disrupting a model-prioritized low-translation-associated RNA G-quadruplex motif increased it by up to 5.8-fold.
Limitation / still unknown
Experimental reporter validation was limited to selected motifs and had n=3, as reported in the figure caption. The model’s transcriptome-wide associations are not individually causal validations. The repressive role of rG4 motifs was previously known for individual cases; the paper’s contribution includes model-prioritized plant 5′-UTR motifs and experimental effects for selected constructs, not first discovery of rG4 biology. Reporter assays do not establish whole-plant phenotype or crop benefit.

Machine-guided synthetic regulatory DNA drives cell-type-specific expression across cell lines and vertebrates

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The CODA platform used the Malinois deep-learning model and sequence-search algorithms to design synthetic cis-regulatory elements (CREs). In massively parallel reporter assays, 94.1% of the synthetic sequences met the authors’ cell-type-specificity criterion, versus 73.6% of model-selected natural sequences and 40.6% of chromatin-mark-selected natural sequences; synthetic sequences also had higher measured target/off-target separation across K562, HepG2 and SK-N-SH cells. In transgenic zebrafish, two of three liver-directed and two of three neuron-directed CREs showed the intended activity. One neuron-directed sequence, synN1, retained cortical and neuronal expression in mice, including postnatal neocortical layer 6 and subplate neurons.

Technology: CODA (Computational Optimization of DNA Activity) with Malinois deep neural network and AdaLead, simulated annealing, and Fast SeqProp sequence search/design algorithms

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Malinois predicted MPRA activity of candidate DNA sequences in K562, HepG2 and SK-N-SH cells; CODA iteratively optimized sequences for specified cell-type specificity. Researchers synthesized and experimentally measured the designs by MPRA, then tested selected CREs with reporter constructs in zebrafish and mice. The paper attributes the novel sequences and their measured expression specificity to this model-guided design loop.
Test and result
In massively parallel reporter assays, 94.1% of the synthetic sequences met the authors’ cell-type-specificity criterion, versus 73.6% of model-selected natural sequences and 40.6% of chromatin-mark-selected natural sequences; synthetic sequences also had higher measured target/off-target separation across K562, HepG2 and SK-N-SH cells.
Limitation / still unknown
The in-vitro work used three transformed human cell lines and reporter assays. In-vivo testing covered a small selected set: two of three liver-directed and two of three neuron-directed elements were active in zebrafish; mouse validation focused on neuronal synN1, with n=3 synN1 mice for postnatal cell-type analysis and n=6 for the 5-week cortical reporter assay. These are transgenic reporter results, not therapeutic delivery or evidence of clinical utility. Earlier synthetic enhancer studies existed; this paper’s counted result is its CODA/Malinois comparison against natural sequences plus selected vertebrate validation, not the general idea of AI-designed enhancers.

CRISPR perturbation and Bayesian network inference map immune-disease regulatory cascades in primary CD4+ T cells

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The study used CRISPR knockouts of 84 genes in primary human CD4+ T cells and a new linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB) network-inference method to estimate 211 regulatory connections. Integrating the inferred network with immune GWAS analyses identified an interconnected module in which KMT2A was inferred upstream of JAK-STAT and IL-2 signaling regulators including IRF4, STAT5A/B and IL2RA, linking an epigenetic regulator to immune-disease-associated pathways.

Technology: Linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB), a Bayesian extension of linear latent causal network inference, applied to CRISPR knockout and RNA-sequencing data

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
LLCB inferred direct and indirect regulatory relationships from perturbation-associated expression effects across 84 targeted genes. The model-derived network and gene-program analysis, combined with immune GWAS statistics, supported the specific KMT2A-to-JAK-STAT/IL-2 regulatory finding. CRISPR perturbation supplied the experimental perturbation data; the network algorithm converted those measurements into the reported regulatory map.
Test and result
The study used CRISPR knockouts of 84 genes in primary human CD4+ T cells and a new linear latent causal Bayes (LLCB) network-inference method to estimate 211 regulatory connections.
Limitation / still unknown
The study perturbed 84 selected genes in primary CD4+ T cells from three donors, so this is not a complete T-cell regulatory map. LLCB “direct effects” are statistical effects adjusted for other perturbed genes and are not evidence of physical binding; effects from unperturbed genes can be attributed to modeled edges. The GWAS integration identifies pathway links, not proof that the inferred cascade causes clinical disease. A prior bioRxiv version (10.1101/2023.09.17.557749) is the same study and is not counted separately.

The paper defined overall survival in checkpoint-treated gastroesophageal cancer as the endpoint. A 123-person MSK cohort supplied initial prognostic-gene filtering. The purported validation cohorts were used for final model selection and therefore do not establish an untouched external test. Drug-sensitivity predictions and cell-line experiments are outside this admitted case, and no therapeutic efficacy is claimed.

27 Sep 2024Tokyo University of Agriculture and Technology

Learned sensor labels reveal different hen behavior transitions across housing

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A learned inertial-sensor classifier was used to compare behavior in cages and floor pens in five laying hens. Floor pens showed more detected transitions involving several comfort and activity behaviors. The small repeated-measure experiment does not establish a general welfare scale, and housing-specific classifier errors may affect comparisons.

Technology: Multilayer perceptron behavior classification from accelerometer and gyroscope features

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The trained multilayer classifier converted sensor streams into behavior labels; conventional temporal counting/statistical comparisons then quantified the source-specific housing contrast.
Test and result
A two-hen labeled training/evaluation step supplied separate housing-specific classifiers. A later recording step used five hens in both housing systems, averaging 4.5 recording days per bird/housing condition. Those later recordings were not reused training data. The source reports more detected transitions involving moving, preening, dust-bathing, litter scratching, resting, tail-wagging and body shaking in floor pens. Visual-scan comparison in a sampled floor-pen video gave correlation .94.
Limitation / still unknown
There were only five birds in the housing comparison; repeated days/intervals are not independent birds. Basic same-bird classification accuracy differed substantially by housing (77.5% cages, 96.3% floor pens), and overlapping sensor windows may affect internal validation. The source does not establish that differential errors cannot explain part of the transition contrast. Training-bird overlap with the later five-bird population is not excluded, although recording data were separate. Pooling days and thresholding transitions do not establish a population-general causal welfare measure. Spatial location came from a colored marker rather than a learned tracking model.

18 Sep 2024University of Washington Institute for Protein Design; University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center; Broad Institute; Massachusetts General Hospital; University of Connecticut; Seoul National University; collaborating institutions

Deep learning identifies previously unreported protein interactions in human bacterial pathogens

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A RoseTTAFold2-Lite pipeline combined residue coevolution, deep-learning complex prediction and AlphaFold modelling to screen protein pairs across 19 human bacterial pathogens. In a validation set selected using the deep-learning pipeline, co-immunoprecipitation detected four of six predicted interactions. Three pairs lacked prior direct interaction evidence: E. coli UbiE–YcaR, P. aeruginosa PA4105–PA4106, and P. aeruginosa WbpG–HisF2. The PA4105–PA4106 structural similarity to proteins in 3-thiaglutamate biosynthesis and the WbpG–HisF2 result provide functional hypotheses, not established native-pathogen mechanisms.

Technology: RoseTTAFold2-Lite integrated with direct coupling analysis and AlphaFold complex modelling

Family AlphaFold: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
RoseTTAFold2-Lite used residue–residue coevolution and predicted complex structures to rank candidate protein pairs in a proteome-wide screen. The authors selected six pairs from the final deep-learning pipeline for co-immunoprecipitation tests; four yielded positive interaction signals. Three were described as lacking previously reported direct interaction evidence, including UbiE–YcaR, PA4105–PA4106 and WbpG–HisF2. The models enabled the experimental target selection; they did not themselves establish physical interactions.
Test and result
In a validation set selected using the deep-learning pipeline, co-immunoprecipitation detected four of six predicted interactions.
Limitation / still unknown
The positive interaction evidence comes from heterologous co-immunoprecipitation/pull-down assays, with two independent experiments per positive pair, rather than native-pathogen systems. The validation subset was small (four positives among six AI-selected candidates); most of the thousands of predicted interactions remain untested, and false positives and false negatives are expected. Proposed roles for PA4105–PA4106 and UbiE–YcaR remain hypotheses; this paper does not establish their physiological function or a therapeutic target.

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

AI contribution
MILTON predicted cases from clinical biomarkers and other quantitative traits, augmenting phenotype labels for genetic association analyses. Test and result
In a phenome-wide analysis of 484,230 genome-sequenced participants, the authors report 182 putative novel gene–disease associations that were not genome-wide significant in baseline cohorts or explained by biomarker associations; 38.9% of the 167 mappable signals were nominally supported with the same direction in FinnGen.

Technology: U-Net segment localization with concurrent CNN features and fully connected perfusion-score estimation

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned network localized myocardial segments and combined image features into scores, enabling the represented clinical expert-agreement and severity-related error analysis.
Test and result
The source retained 1,288 people from J-ACCESS 3/4 and analyzed stress/rest volumes separately. Expert 17-segment perfusion grades trained a U-Net/CNN scorer. Two twenty-volume validation/test sets exchanged roles, yielding forty reported test studies and 680 segment comparisons. Exact segment agreement was 79.6%; error increased with defect severity and was worse in the female dataset.
Limitation / still unknown
The paper inconsistently calls doubled stress/rest data patients and reports differing scan totals; patient-level isolation of paired scans across training/validation/test is not established. Exchanging validation and test roles compromises an untouched-test interpretation. Ninety-six percent of source segments were normal or mildly abnormal, so aggregate agreement does not establish sensitivity for severe disease. Expert interpretation is the reference, not invasive disease truth or measured subsequent prognosis. The test is small and no clinical benefit was demonstrated.

Among 218 randomized participants, interpretable paired videos were available for 67 tandem-walk and 56 natural-walk participants. StarDist was trained on manually annotated human and mouse pancreatic-cancer-organoid images. Learned segmentation enabled image-derived counts, area and size-group trajectories during experimental treatment. The source reports greater gemcitabine-associated effects in larger organoids and comparison with an endpoint viability assay. The represented finding is a measured size-response pattern in experimental models, rather than segmentation accuracy alone.
Limitation / still unknown
Small model panels and image-derived measurements limit generalization. Healthy/unhealthy labels were assigned by a fixed intensity threshold after segmentation, not learned biological-state classification; debris and merging affect counts. Endpoint viability and imaging disagreed in immune-cell co-cultures, so no secure immune-mediated killing or immunotherapy-potency claim is adopted. Operational culture/treatment procedures and independent assay replication were not adjudicated.

The source split 634 prostatectomy patients into 507 development and 127 test patients. No paired clinical reader-assistance or treatment-benefit trial was performed, and no general superiority is claimed.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: The researchers combined personalized gut-microbiome community metabolic models from human iHMP data with tree-based machine-learning feature selection to identify microbial strains and metabolites associated with ulcerative-colitis samples. Parabacteroides merdae ATCC 43,184 and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine were among the most predictive features; the strain was also the main modeled microbial contributor to the metabolite. In a DSS-induced mouse colitis experiment, oral administration of the bacterium or metabolite improved reported colitis measures.

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Personalized community metabolic models estimated strain-level contributions to secreted metabolites in human iHMP samples. Tree-based classifiers selected discriminative strain and metabolite features; XGBRF feature attribution ranked P. merdae ATCC 43,184 and N-acetyl-D-mannosamine highly, motivating the mouse validation. Test and result
In a DSS-induced mouse colitis experiment, oral administration of the bacterium or metabolite improved reported colitis measures.

AI contribution
The learned adversarial translation transformed non-attenuation-corrected SPECT images into PET-like representations, enabling the represented patient-level comparison of regional attenuation artifacts and correction failures against an imaging reference.
Test and result
Seventy-one patients had matched SPECT/PET examinations. Thirty-one supplied image-level training/validation data; forty different patients supplied the clinical test set. Internal training/validation images were randomly split within thirty-one patients, rather than a demonstrated patient-separated validation split. Training SPECT/PET scans could be separated by up to three years; test scans were separated by roughly forty-six days on average. Single-center selection, small and biased clinical subgroups, consensus readers and reference-scan temporal differences limit generalization. Some image-error metrics worsened and reduced significance against PET is not proof of equivalence. True-defect erasure prevents any claim of uniformly safe correction. No clinical outcome, radiation-dose benefit or replacement utility was established.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

In 29,257 participants, the quantitative mJSW phenotype had substantially higher SNP heritability than the binary phenotypes and yielded 18 genome-wide-significant loci, compared with one for the image-based binary classifier and six for ICD-10 coding; only one mJSW locus was already significant in a large prior knee-OA GWAS. Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The neural networks converted routine knee DXA scans into two disease phenotypes: a case–control OA classifier and a quantitative minimum joint-space-width measurement. The researchers used these AI-derived phenotypes in GWAS and downstream epidemiological association analyses, increasing statistical power and revealing genetic and fracture associations that were not significant with ICD-10 case coding or the binary classifier.
Test and result
Using knee DXA scans from the UK Biobank, a ResNet-101 model identified 1,931 more probable knee-osteoarthritis cases than health-record coding and a U-Net segmentation model estimated minimum joint-space width (mJSW).
Limitation / still unknown
The GWAS used 29,257 quality-controlled UK Biobank participants with knee DXA images, all from the analyzed white-British ancestry subset; ancestry transferability is unestablished. DXA images were non-weight-bearing. The 18 loci are genome-wide associations for a model-derived quantitative endophenotype, not 18 proven causal OA genes; the paper notes only one also reached significance in a previous large knee-OA GWAS and many loci overlap broad anthropometric associations. The fracture result is observational and does not show that OA or joint-space narrowing causes fractures. The medRxiv preprint DOI 10.1101/2023.03.07.23286909 is an earlier version of this same study and is not counted separately.

12 Jun 2023Gladstone Institutes; University of California, San Francisco; Chan Zuckerberg Biohub San Francisco

SIMMER-guided experiments identify gut bacterial strains that deplete methotrexate

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: SIMMER combines reaction-chemistry and protein-sequence similarity to predict gut microbial species and enzymes responsible for drug biotransformations. For methotrexate (MTX), the model predicted candidate strains and enzyme sequences; researchers tested 42 gut bacterial isolates by HPLC. SIMMER predicted 13 isolates as MTX-metabolizing, and 10 of those tested isolates showed MTX depletion; the association was significant in the study (Fisher exact p=0.046). Predicted MTX-hydrolysis enzyme signatures were also enriched in stool samples of MTX nonresponders in an analyzed rheumatoid-arthritis cohort.

Technology: SIMMER, a computational reaction-similarity and protein-homology pipeline using chemical fingerprints, MetaCyc reactions and gut metagenomic sequences

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
SIMMER proposed specific bacterial species and enzyme sequences for known drug transformations. The team tested its MTX predictions against an independent panel of 42 gut bacterial isolates and HPLC-measured drug depletion, and compared predicted enzyme presence with baseline stool metagenomes and later MTX response in an RA dataset.
Test and result
For methotrexate (MTX), the model predicted candidate strains and enzyme sequences; researchers tested 42 gut bacterial isolates by HPLC.
Limitation / still unknown
The study reports species-level evidence for bacterial MTX depletion, but the enzyme predictions themselves were not individually purified or functionally validated. Only 13 of 42 tested isolates were predicted positive and 10 depleted MTX; predictions may have false positives, as the authors note. The RA association is observational and does not establish that microbial metabolism caused treatment nonresponse. The underlying fact that gut bacteria can metabolize MTX was already known; this result concerns species-level prediction and validation, not discovery of MTX metabolism itself.

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The three learned selectors prioritized a shared measured-expression marker set after broad filtering, enabling the represented candidate-pattern and subsequent source-described case-control comparison. Immune deconvolution or network diagrams alone are not the admission basis.
Test and result
The analysis combined GSE26378 and GSE26440, with primary series metadata listing 180 septic-shock and 53 normal-control blood-expression profiles in total. Differential/module filtering preceded RF, SVM-RFE and tenfold-tuned LASSO selection. Their intersection identified CYSTM1, MMP8 and CD177. The paper reports increased expression and discrimination in GSE13904, a separately indexed pediatric inflammatory-spectrum dataset.
Limitation / still unknown
Distinct series/sample identifiers do not prove independent people. GSE13904 includes inflammatory-response, sepsis and septic-shock samples; the exact analytic subset and repeated-person separation were not independently reconstructed. Feature filtering used clinical labels before selection, and healthy-control contrasts do not establish real-world diagnostic specificity. Source prose twice refers to rheumatoid arthritis despite the sepsis analysis; no RA result is adopted. MMP8/CD177 links to sepsis were already known, and CYSTM1 remains a candidate association without functional or therapeutic validation. Reported ROC/decision curves do not demonstrate clinical benefit.

Technology: TrueFidelity deep neural network reconstruction trained on high-quality filtered-back-projection images

Editorial relevance 47 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The pretrained neural reconstruction selectively suppressed image noise in actual patient acquisitions, enabling the paired clinical test of image-quality and plaque-contour tradeoffs across reconstruction strengths.
Test and result
Prospective single-center enrollment yielded 51 patients and 714 reconstructed datasets. Each acquisition was reconstructed using filtered back-projection, ten ASiR-V strengths and three learned reconstruction strengths. Two experienced radiologists, blinded to reconstruction protocol, assessed four selected reconstructions in consensus, with randomized reading order and separated sessions. Medium-strength DLIR had the highest subjective plaque-image quality; high-strength DLIR had lower noise but did not significantly outperform maximum-strength ASiR-V on the reported objective noise, SNR and CNR comparisons.
Limitation / still unknown
One vendor and center, selected subjective comparison datasets, consensus readers without separate-reader reproducibility, and exclusion of severe motion or high heart rates limit generalization. No invasive coronary reference was routinely available, so agreement between image reconstructions does not establish diagnostic accuracy. No radiation-dose reduction, patient outcome benefit or dedicated stent subgroup result was tested.

Technology: Genetic-algorithm feature selection with gradient boosting; fully connected deep neural network classification

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned feature selection and nonlinear classification linked preoperative record patterns to measured/coded postoperative outcomes, providing a specific retrospective clinical evaluation beyond a generic architecture benchmark. No discovered causal risk factor or clinical intervention effect is adopted.
Test and result
The source derived 541,354 procedure records from 392,661 patients, using prior diagnosis/medication windows and coded VTE within thirty days. A 70:30 random procedure split evaluated a six-hidden-layer DNN. Final Table 6 reports AUC 0.901 after genetic feature selection versus 0.780 using established risk factors. The abstract instead cites 0.873, which main text assigns to a preliminary feature-selection stage.
Limitation / still unknown
Patients could contribute multiple procedures, and patient-level partition isolation was not established. Broad procedure-code ranges may include operations beyond hip/knee replacement. Genetic selection/tuning isolation from final evaluation remains unclear; excluding postoperative prophylaxis also limits preoperative applicability. The Table6/abstract difference is not silently resolved. Drug-feature importance is associational and does not establish medication harms or benefit from changing treatment.

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Pretrained neural segmentation converted patient CT scans into quantitative lung features used with clinical variables in the represented mortality score; learned risk modeling and binning enabled the patient-outcome discrimination analysis.
Test and result
A multicenter first-wave dataset was reduced from 1,575 enrolled patients to 1,125 complete records, including 292 deaths. Repeated train/test splits and repeated cross-validation compared candidate models and selected a five-variable logistic model. Pretrained learned segmentation enabled automated lung measurements. A later, prospectively collected single-center cohort of 213 patients, including 31 deaths, yielded AUC 0.808 with reported 95% confidence interval 0.740–0.877.
Limitation / still unknown
Prospective cohort collection does not establish that the model and thresholds were fixed before its outcomes were known. Complete-case selection, different pandemic waves, one-center later validation and historical treatment conditions limit transportability. The paper inconsistently describes 213 versus 214 validation patients and presents four low-risk deaths as 1.8% without a clearly appropriate low-risk denominator; those percentages and post-hoc exclusions are not adopted here. Supplemental acquisition/endpoint details were not independently read. No causal CT mechanism, intervention benefit or current clinical utility is established.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Observed hospital mortality differed between groups and remained associated after statistical adjustment. This is a retrospective cohort relationship, without established biological subtypes, causal treatment effects or validated bedside deployment.

Technology: Unsupervised K-means clustering of routine ICU clinical measurements

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
K-means learned multivariable patient groups without using mortality as its clustering target; subsequent outcome analysis linked those learned groups to observed hospital mortality. PCA visualization alone and recovery of known individual severity markers are not the represented result.
Test and result
The source selected 8,817 MIMIC-IV sepsis patients and used eleven expert-selected variables measured during the first ICU day. It compared two-to-eight clusters and selected two using clustering criteria. Hospital mortality was 29.4% in the smaller group versus 8.5% in the larger group; adjusted odds ratio was 2.214, 95% CI 1.780–2.754. Outcome differences are actual cohort observations beyond cluster-separation scores.
Limitation / still unknown
The groups were derived and compared in the same retrospective single-center database, without external transportability testing. They may reflect severity and clinical heterogeneity rather than distinct biological entities. Missing lactate and oxygenation values required imputation; absent baseline SOFA and unmeasured infection characteristics may bias case definition and associations. No causal therapy-response difference, prospective prediction or operational benefit was shown.

Neural phase-label flickering tracks atypical courses in a small surgical-video study

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Researchers found that unstable phase labels from a pretrained surgical-video network coincided with complicated or atypical courses in fifteen recorded operations. Flicker measures and thresholds were developed on the same videos, so the result does not establish an independently validated complication detector or better clinical documentation.

Technology: TeCNO convolutional temporal surgical-phase recognition with post-hoc flicker analysis

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The neural network generated time-ordered surgical-phase predictions; instability in those learned predictions exposed the represented association with atypical observed operative courses. The reporting interface itself is not treated as a scientific discovery.
Test and result
TeCNO was trained on 52 surgical videos and applied to fifteen further cholecystectomy videos, independently phase-annotated by a highly experienced surgeon. Investigators then reviewed unstable label clusters and derived flicker thresholds on those same fifteen cases. The source reports that threshold rules identified five of six apparently divergent courses; one gallbladder perforation produced no substantial flicker increase.
Limitation / still unknown
Post-hoc pattern recognition, same-cohort cutoff derivation and a very small event count create substantial optimism and selection risk. Independent blinded complication adjudication and external alert validation were not established. Phase-annotation agreement, report generation and exploratory event association do not demonstrate complete or safer operative documentation, real-time deployment, improved outcomes or reliable detection of specific complication types.

GANs learn the high-dimensional joint distribution of plant presence and supply conditional co-occurrence estimates that describe how associations change when additional species are present.

GAN models learned joint species-presence distributions from 5153 recorded vegetation patches. Generated composition abundance and soil-affinity patterns were compared with the observed data; higher-order conditional association estimates were derived from generated configurations.
Limitation / still unknown
The specific third- and fourth-order conditional frequencies were not independently checked in held-out field data. Generated patches and repeated model initializations are not independent field replication. Co-occurrence does not prove competition, facilitation or other mechanisms. 28 Feb 2022University of Portsmouth; Portsmouth Hospitals University NHS Trust

Learned postoperative records distinguish readmission in a colorectal-surgery cohort

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A bidirectional LSTM classifier was evaluated for readmission using records from 4,336 colorectal-surgery patients. The source reports internal discrimination with an 80:20 training/test split, using perioperative and postoperative information. The result is a retrospective clinical model evaluation, without established preoperative prediction, external validation or demonstrated benefit from changing surgical care.

Technology: Bidirectional LSTM classifier applied to reshaped clinical patient records

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned classifier combined clinical-record features to discriminate observed readmission labels, supplying the represented retrospective outcome-evaluation result. Conventional descriptive associations with surgical approaches are not attributed to AI discovery.
Test and result
A prospectively maintained surgical database covered 4,336 operations during 2003–2019, including 321 readmissions. The paper compared multiple classifiers and describes an 80:20 split for readmission analysis. Its three-hidden-layer bidirectional LSTM reportedly achieved sensitivity 84.1% and specificity 90.9%. Predictor candidates included clinical, operative and postoperative variables; a reduced set retained length of stay and operative details.
Limitation / still unknown
Prospective database maintenance does not make model evaluation prospective. Feature selection and preprocessing isolation from testing are incompletely specified, and no external or temporal test was reported. Inclusion of postoperative variables prevents a preoperative risk claim; the permissible prediction time and all-variable leakage risks are not fully established. The reported 87.5% accuracy equals the mean of reported sensitivity and specificity, so it is not adopted as an authenticated population-weighted accuracy. Reshaping records for LSTM does not establish genuine longitudinal sequence learning. No causal effect of surgical approach or improvement in care was tested.

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The LSTM learned nonlinear dependencies across baseline and follow-up clinical/imaging measurements, enabling the represented patient-endpoint discrimination beyond the separately assessed regression and feed-forward models.
Test and result
A retrospective imaging substudy of a prospectively enrolled three-center stroke cohort retained 598 patients with baseline and follow-up CT, including twenty malignant-edema endpoints: twelve decompressive hemicraniectomies and eight deaths with midline shift of at least five millimeters. The main Methods describe nested stratified tenfold cross-validation with patients held out from training/tuning. Limitation / still unknown
Only twenty positive events and selection for available repeat imaging leave substantial uncertainty about transportability and overfitting. External cohorts, prospective locked-model evaluation and clinical decision benefit were not tested. The outcome combines a clinical intervention decision with edema-related death; CT and clinical assessment timing varied. Supplemental implementation/imputation details were not independently read, so fold-specific preprocessing isolation is not authenticated here. Model feature attribution is predictive association, not causal edema biology.

iTARGEX analysis identifies ELG1 as a regulator of yeast transcription buffering and four protein-turnover regulators

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Experiments supported ELG1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of transcriptional buffering during S phase; the phenotype was reproduced in a second genetic background and rescued by a PCNA-D150E mutation. Follow-up protein-turnover measurements showed altered turnover in MRN1, UPF3, RAM1 and SSN3 deletion strains.

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
iTARGEX associated gene-expression profiles from deletion strains with biological traits without requiring prior gene annotations and nominated candidate regulators. The researchers then performed S-phase transcription and protein-turnover experiments to test the model-prioritized candidates, supporting ELG1's role in transcriptional buffering and altered turnover for four deletion strains.
Test and result
Experiments supported ELG1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of transcriptional buffering during S phase; the phenotype was reproduced in a second genetic background and rescued by a PCNA-D150E mutation.
Limitation / still unknown
The study used budding yeast and pre-existing deletion-mutant transcriptome profiles, followed by experiments on selected candidates. ELG1's role in S-phase transcription buffering was reproduced in a second yeast genetic background and rescued by PCNA-D150E; the protein-turnover effects concern yeast deletion strains. These results do not establish corresponding human functions.

8 Jun 2021University of Oxford; University of Coimbra; University of North Carolina at Greensboro; University of Algarve; Gorongosa National Park

Satellite-image clustering guides discovery of four late Miocene fossil sites in Mozambique’s Urema Rift

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park. The 2018 campaign documented four new late Miocene fossil localities; three lay within the model’s target cluster and the fourth was less than 90 m away in the same gully system. Together, the sites expose the first reported estuarine coastal-forest fossil setting in the East African Rift System, filling a regional paleoenvironmental gap.

Technology: Unsupervised k-means clustering of Landsat 8 imagery

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The authors clustered seven spectral bands without pre-labeled land-cover classes, compared clusters with known fossil localities, and selected the cluster containing most known sites as a predictive target for field prospecting. This decision-support workflow directed the 2018 field survey that documented the new localities; a random forest was separately used to estimate spectral-band importance.
Test and result
Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park.
Limitation / still unknown
This was a pilot study in a 36 km² area and the model had notable false positives: reported precision was 55.56%, despite 84.6% overall accuracy. Three of four new localities overlapped the selected cluster; the fourth was less than 90 m away and was found by surveying the same gully system, so model localization for that site is indirect. The findings are four new fossil localities, not four new hominin taxa; the reported estuarine coastal-forest interpretation is a paleoenvironmental inference.

30 May 2021Ruhr University Bochum; Technische Hochschule Georg Agricola

Learned OCT texture analysis distinguishes sampled brain-metastasis tissue from healthy tissue

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A support-vector classifier separated OCT images of sampled brain metastases and healthy brain tissue using histology-derived labels. The analysis retained fourteen tissue samples from a twenty-patient collection. Reported image-level accuracy is exploratory: cross-validation split B-scans, without demonstrated separation of tissue samples or patients, and does not establish surgical diagnostic performance.

Technology: Support-vector machines on OCT texture features with PCA dimensionality reduction

Editorial relevance 33 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The SVM combined learned boundaries over multifeature OCT texture measurements to discriminate histology-labeled sampled tissue categories, supplying a specific ex-vivo diagnostic feasibility result. PCA alone is not treated as the enabling AI contribution.
Test and result
Twenty patients contributed twenty-two tissue samples; histologic purity criteria retained ten tumor and four healthy samples. An experienced neuropathologist assigned tissue-composition reference labels. Texture features from 14,336 OCT B-scans were reduced with PCA and classified using grid-tuned SVMs with tenfold cross-validation. The source reports up to 96.83% image-level discrimination of pooled vital/necrotic tumor versus healthy tissue.
Limitation / still unknown
B-scans from the same tissue specimen are correlated, and the described allocation does not establish specimen-level or patient-level separation between folds. Normalization/PCA isolation and nested tuning are not established. Purity-selected specimens and small sample counts constrain interpretation; thousands of images do not substitute for independent patients. No intraoperative clinical deployment, margin-level ground truth, recurrence reduction or survival benefit was demonstrated.

Finding: A convolutional neural network analyzed urine-output trends in 35,573 ICU patients to estimate later severe kidney-injury events under a restrictive urine-plus-creatinine definition. Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The CNN learned temporal urine-output features linked to later recorded severe-AKI labels and was compared with a logistic baseline. The admitted result is specific retrospective clinical discrimination, not recovery of a single urine-output cutoff or a validated intervention.
Test and result
The source pooled eICU and MIMIC-III records and separated patients across training, validation, calibration and test sets. The CNN used twelve-hour urine-output windows, with case series truncated six hours before the defined event. Limitation / still unknown
This was retrospective pooled-database evaluation, not a locked prospective clinical test. Urine output contributes to both model input and event definition; imputation and restrictive exclusions limit generalization to broader AKI. Reported likelihood ratios must not be read as positive predictive value or five true cases per six alarms. Individual-record timing, exact alarm yield and calibrated probabilities were not independently reconstructed. No reduced kidney injury, mortality or treatment benefit was demonstrated.

12 Apr 2021Ghent University; VIB Center for Plant Systems Biology; Bioinformatics Institute Ghent

An integrated Arabidopsis regulatory network predicts 13 previously unlinked reactive-oxygen-stress regulators

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Researchers integrated DNA-motif, chromatin-accessibility, TF-binding and expression evidence with supervised learning to build an Arabidopsis gene-regulatory network of 1,491 transcription factors and 1.7 million TF–target interactions. The network predicted candidate reactive-oxygen-species (ROS) regulators; loss- and gain-of-function phenotyping supported 13 regulators not previously linked to ROS or stress responses. Newly tested examples included WRKY55, WRKY47, AT2G33710 and AT5G57150. The paper also reports that 75% of its ROS-predicted TFs had ROS or physiological stress functions supported by either this study or prior evidence.

This is retrospective clinical model validation, without proven preventive benefit or prospective clinical deployment.

Technology: Stochastic gradient-boosted decision trees for time-dependent dementia-risk prediction

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The trained GBM combined multimodal baseline features into time-dependent risk estimates; its concrete external clinical evaluation exposed the effect of cohort composition on reported performance. Propensity-score matching alone is not treated as the enabling AI contribution.
Test and result
A feature-restricted GBM was retrained on ADNI to match available AddNeuroMed measurements, retaining thirty-two clinical, imaging and genetic features. It was then evaluated in 244 initially normal or mildly impaired AddNeuroMed participants, thirty of whom later received a dementia diagnosis. The reported external concordance index was approximately 0.81. Across one hundred propensity-score matchings, the average matched set contained 164 participants and twenty conversions, with concordance approximately 0.88.
Limitation / still unknown
External evaluation was retrospective; prospective cohort follow-up does not establish predictor locking before clinical outcomes were known. Only thirty external events and fewer at long horizons limit precision. Matching changes the selected population and can improve apparent performance without improving the model or eliminating all bias. The revised model differs from the earlier full-feature model. No clinical prevention, treatment selection, economic benefit or general-population diagnostic utility was demonstrated.

AI contribution

Editorial relevance 40 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The learned residual networks restored projection information before reconstruction, enabling the represented within-cohort test of clinical perfusion-measurement agreement under reduced data.
Test and result
A prospectively collected 363-person clinical cohort supplied full-acquisition list-mode data. Shorter-time data used the first half of acquisition events, while fewer-projection data omitted alternate views. Residual networks learned projection restoration; the source describes tenfold cross-validation on the cohort. Reconstructed clinical perfusion measures, including total perfusion deficit, were compared with full acquisitions using commercial quantitative software and agreement analyses. Learned reconstructions reduced measured bias relative to uncorrected reduced data.
Limitation / still unknown
Reduced acquisitions were derived from the same full scans, rather than separate real-world short scans. Full-acquisition reconstruction is a measurement reference, not independent disease truth. Detailed fold-specific preprocessing/tuning isolation is not established. Gated functional performance, diagnostic decisions, patient outcomes and actual lower-dose acquisition were not tested. Some headline image-metric labels and dispersion values are inconsistent, so they are not adopted as precise comparative claims.

In colorectal-cancer cells, it associated depletion of olfactory receptors and TGFβ/WNT pathway genes with abnormal multicellular organization. The authors integrated the predictions with patient data and found olfactory-receptor expression correlated with WNT/TGFβ signatures and worse outcomes in higher-grade tumors.

Technology: KCML, weakly supervised machine-learning framework using support-vector-machine classifiers trained on gene-ontology annotations and high-throughput perturbation phenotypes

Editorial relevance 53 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Mapped gene-perturbation morphology to context-specific gene functions and nominated olfactory-receptor links to multicellular organization; patient-expression analyses provided an independent association check.
Test and result
Knowledge- and Context-driven Machine Learning (KCML) analyzed perturbation phenotypes across molecular, cellular and population scales.
Limitation / still unknown
Patient data validate expression associations and outcome stratification, not a causal olfactory-receptor mechanism in tumors. The authors describe KCML as hypothesis-generating; predictions can be indirect through interacting genes. This is a distinct paper/result from later AI cancer models.

4 Mar 2020Google DeepMind

Predicted structures of SARS-CoV-2 proteins

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: DeepMind openly shared AlphaFold predictions, without waiting for review, for six poorly studied viral proteins (membrane, ORF3a, Nsp2, Nsp4, Nsp6, and the C-terminal domain of papain-like protease). They were not experimentally verified; an ORF3a experimental structure deposited in the PDB in June 2020 matched the second predicted model well.

Technology: AlphaFold

Family AlphaFold: profile · models page

Editorial relevance 67 biology Original source Suggest a correction

Publication: Announcement only · Test context: prospective or independent check. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
AlphaFold free-modelling predicted structures for six understudied SARS-CoV-2 proteins, with per-residue confidence scores.
Test and result
Predictions compared with experimental structures: the spike prediction matched the PDB structure, and the second-ranked ORF3a model agreed well with later experimental work.
Limitation / still unknown
Predictions were not experimentally verified overall; the system was still in development and accuracy is not certain; released before peer review; the top ORF3a model misplaced some transmembrane helices.

22 Jan 2020University of California San Diego; and collaborators

Interpretable multi-omics machine learning reveals unexpected drug mechanisms in Huntington disease models

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An interpretable machine-learning model integrated transcriptomic, epigenomic, metabolomic and proteomic data from Huntington-disease cell models to identify previously unknown mechanisms for protective compounds. The analysis predicted autophagy activation for one compound group and mitochondrial-respiration inhibition for another; follow-up imaging, biochemical and energetics assays experimentally confirmed these effects in the cell model.

Technology: Interpretable network-optimization model integrating multi-omics over a molecular-interaction network

Editorial relevance 60 biology Original sourcePaper Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The model integrated multiple omics and prioritized cellular pathways as candidate mechanisms of action; researchers tested those predictions with cellular imaging, biochemical assays and energetics measurements. It revealed unexpected mechanisms for compounds with unrelated known targets.
Test and result
The analysis predicted autophagy activation for one compound group and mitochondrial-respiration inhibition for another; follow-up imaging, biochemical and energetics assays experimentally confirmed these effects in the cell model.
Limitation / still unknown
Findings were experimentally established in STHdhQ111 murine striatal cells, with autophagy effects also checked in human SH-SY5Y and HEK293 cell lines. The paper notes that the model prioritizes pathways but does not resolve every causal step or demonstrate therapeutic efficacy in patients.
